sentences.text: Chart scale confuses people, because large and small seem backward.
Scale is the ratio of a distance on the chart to the same distance on the earth.
One to forty thousand is a larger scale than one to eighty thousand.
Each inch covers less ground, so it shows more detail.
Here’s the handle: large scale, large detail, small area.
Now the chart types, from the smallest scale to the largest.
Sailing charts, for planning offshore passages.
General charts, for coastwise navigation well offshore.
Coast charts, for inshore work and entering bays.
Harbor charts, for harbors, anchorages and small waterways.
And small-craft charts, like the strip charts that follow the Intracoastal Waterway.
So which chart do you use?
Always the largest scale available for the water you’re in.
More detail is never a problem.
